learningObjective: Compute the arithmetic intensity of a batched matrix multiplication and compare it against a GPU's ridge point to determine bind regime.
stem: Consider a single-tile FP16 GEMM C = A · B with A ∈ ℝ^{M×K}, B ∈ ℝ^{K×N}, C ∈ ℝ^{M×N}, M=N=K=1024, all tensors streamed once from HBM (no persistence). On A100 SXM (FP16 Tensor Core peak ≈ 312 TFLOP/s, HBM ≈ 2.0 TB/s, ridge point ≈ 156 FLOP/byte), which classification is correct?

options.text: Compute-bound: FLOPs = 2·M·N·K ≈ 2.15 G; bytes moved ≈ (M·K + K·N + M·N)·2 ≈ 6.29 MB; AI ≈ 342 FLOP/byte, above the FP16 ridge of ~156, so the ceiling is the FP16 Tensor Core peak of ~312 TFLOP/s.
Memory-bound: even at K=1024, streaming the operands limits performance; AI ≈ 1 FLOP/byte because each element of A and B is loaded once and reused only during the tile computation.
Compute-bound only for FP32 accumulation, but memory-bound for FP16 accumulation because the accumulator halves the effective register file and forces spilling to HBM.
Undetermined without knowing the launch grid; the same math on the same GPU can flip compute/memory regimes depending on how many blocks are launched.

explanation: GEMM FLOPs = 2·M·N·K = 2·1024^3 ≈ 2.147 × 10^9. Bytes for reading A, B and writing C = (1024·1024 + 1024·1024 + 1024·1024) · 2 B = 6.29 MB. Arithmetic intensity = 2.147e9 / 6.29e6 ≈ 341 FLOP/byte. This is above the A100 FP16 Tensor Core ridge point (~156 FLOP/byte), so the operation is compute-bound and the achievable ceiling is the FP16 Tensor Core peak (~312 TFLOP/s). Reaching that ceiling requires efficient tiling; the classification itself is bounded by the AI vs ridge comparison.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: AI = 2·M·N·K / ((M·K+K·N+M·N)·2) ≈ 341 FLOP/byte, which exceeds the FP16 ridge point; ceiling is FP16 Tensor Core peak.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: AI ≈ 1 FLOP/byte is characteristic of GEMV (batch=1), not GEMM with K=1024. GEMM has strong on-tile reuse.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: FP16 vs FP32 accumulation affects Tensor Core selection and accuracy, not the Roofline classification via HBM traffic. Register file spilling to HBM is not what defines the compute/memory regime here.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: Roofline classification for a well-formed GEMM is a function of AI vs ridge point; launch grid affects achieved efficiency, not the compute/memory-bound category.

assumptions: Operands are loaded from HBM exactly once through a tiled schedule; the arithmetic intensity is measured against HBM traffic.
No exotic streaming (e.g., persistent kernels reusing weights across steps) that would change effective bytes moved.
nonImplications: Does not imply the kernel will reach the ~312 TFLOP/s ceiling; achieving that requires good tiling, occupancy, and MMA scheduling.
Does not imply that reducing K further (e.g., K=1) would remain compute-bound: shrinking K reduces AI proportionally.

distractorRationales.B: Confuses GEMV traffic pattern with GEMM tile reuse.
distractorRationales.C: Introduces an accumulation-precision fiction unrelated to Roofline classification.
distractorRationales.D: Vacuous 'undetermined' claim contradicted by well-defined AI vs ridge comparison.
